subject: Fastlane: account settlement options after service degradation
messages:
From: Amaya Cho <amaya.cho@fastlane.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@fastlane.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production degradation 7/24 - request for settlement options

Laura —

We experienced significant degradation in the Redwood inference endpoint serving our fastlane-prod model on 7/24 between ~02:40–05:15 UTC. Symptoms: sustained 5xx spike (~7% errors over peak hour), median latency jumping from ~120ms to ~1.2s, and a 40% drop in successful throughput for our busiest route. Our SREs captured traces and logs; I've attached the raw logs (Fastlane_ProdLogs_20270724.zip).

This incident materially impacted an automated customer workflow and triggered downstream refunds on our side. We need to understand Redwood's proposed commercial recourse: credit calculation methodology, whether a one-time service extension is possible, and any immediate mitigation steps you can offer. We'd like an executive-level call this week (Amaya + Jordan + Fastlane procurement + Redwood execs) to align on a path forward.

Please confirm receipt and next steps. We can share additional telemetry if needed.

Attachments: Fastlane_ProdLogs_20270724.zip (application/zip)

Thanks,
Amaya
Head of Platform Reliability
Fastlane AI
amaya.cho@fastlane.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amaya Cho <amaya.cho@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation 7/24 - request for settlement options

Hi Amaya — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We saw the same spike in our monitoring and I apologize for the disruption. I want to get you clear options and a proposed timeline before the exec call. Quick plan: 

1) Dev will provide a short RCA and a quantification of the SLO breaches (token/route-level).
2) Ben will assemble a commercial proposal with an explicit credit calculation and an alternative offer (trial of Dedicated capacity / discounted reserved burst).
3) I'll schedule the exec alignment call and include our legal/finance contacts as needed.

Ben — can you draft a one-page settlement options doc (PDF) for Fastlane that lays out: credit calculation (per-token and per-minute adjustments), an optional one-time account credit, and an alternative of a 30-day Dedicated trial at a reduced rate? Attach the draft as "proposed_settlement_terms_v1.pdf".

Dev — priority: share the initial SLO numbers we observed and any mitigations we've applied. Rishi/Marcus, FYI and please flag anything I should escalate to leadership.

Amaya — I'll propose times for an exec call in a separate calendar invite. Expect a preliminary proposal from Ben by end of day Monday.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Amaya Cho <amaya.cho@fastlane.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation 7/24 - request for settlement options

Laura / team — preliminary notes from infra: 

- Timeline: 2027-07-24 02:37–05:12 UTC correlated with an autoscaling regression on the GPU pool serving the region. Some warm caches were evicted during a rapid scale-down, causing a cascade of longer KV cache warmups.
- Impact: 5xx rate peaked at 7.2% for 03:10–03:40 UTC. Median generation latency for route /v1/fastlane-gen rose from baseline 120ms to 1.2s (p50) and p95 to ~4.8s during the worst window. Throughput for the API key associated with Fastlane dropped ~38% (successful completions) during the same window.
- Corrections applied: reverted the autoscaler policy change and added temporary sticky warmers to reduce cache thrash. We're pushing a runtime patch to better handle rapid scale-downs; target rollout by 07/26 EOD.

I've attached the extracted SLO metrics: fastlane_slo_metrics_20270724.csv (includes per-route error/latency/throughput breakdowns). I'll follow up with a short RCA doc once the patch validation completes.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amaya Cho <amaya.cho@fastlane.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 08:59:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation 7/24 - request for settlement options

Amaya — appreciate the quick signal and the logs. We've pulled together three options for Fastlane; attaching a short one-pager (proposed_settlement_terms_v1.pdf) with the numbers but summarizing here: 

Option A — Calculated credit:
- Method: prorated credit based on measured SLA shortfall for the affected route(s) during the incident window. Using our standard per-token and per-minute billing, estimated credit = $38,450. (Details in PDF.)

Option B — Account credit + priority remediation:
- One-time account credit of $25,000 + guaranteed priority handling for next 30 days (priority routing, weekly runbook reviews, and dedicated SRE contact).

Option C — Dedicated trial and migration support:
- 30-day trial of a small Redwood Dedicated pool for Fastlane (discounted 50% for the first month) plus migration assistance. If Fastlane purchases a committed Dedicated plan within 60 days, Redwood will apply a $20k transition credit toward the commitment.

Next steps I propose: pick the option you prefer and we convert to a short amendment/statement of work. If you want to accept Option A as a pure credit, we can issue it within 7 business days after an acceptance email. If you'd like an amendment for Option C, we can draft a DocuSign with PO terms for signature.

Attachments: proposed_settlement_terms_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Would you be available for an exec alignment call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT? Laura will send the invite.

Best,
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts — West
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0123
From: Amaya Cho <amaya.cho@fastlane.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@fastlane.ai>, Procurement Ops <procure@fastlane.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation 7/24 - request for settlement options

Ben / Laura — thanks for the clear options and the quick analysis, and thanks Dev for the RCA summary. Fastlane prefers Option B (one-time account credit + priority remediation) as it balances immediate operational support and cash reconciliation. A few clarifying asks before we sign off: 

- Can you confirm the exact scope of “priority handling” (SLA for triage, cadence of status updates, named SRE contact)?
- We need the credit applied to our August invoice; can you confirm acceptance timeline so our finance team can process it?
- For internal compliance we require a brief amendment (1 page) that we can countersign. If you send a DocuSign link we can get procurement to review same-day.

If you can address those items, we can move to acceptance today. We also want to lock a joint post-mortem session next week to validate the runtime patch once it's live.

Amaya
Head of Platform Reliability, Fastlane AI
